note: June Suddaby's own street lines: once a day each (3.6.3). 30 needed, 102 written.

lines.text: You'll be the new owner. I'm June.
So you're the new owner. I'm not stopping.
The new owner. Another time. I'm late.
Morning. The new owner, I take it.
I'm June. You'll want to know that.
New owner. We'll talk. Not now.
Evening, new owner. I'm leaving soon, so be quick.
New owner, you're getting wet. Move.
So you're the new owner. I'll not keep you.
Nowak. Let's keep it brief.
Mr Nowak. I've a train to see about.
Morning, Nowak. You look as if you've not slept.
Nowak. Don't make it a thing.
Afternoon, Nowak. I'm packing.
Nowak. If you need anything, ask Sheila, not me.
Nowak. I'll say it once: be careful.
Evening, Nowak. I can't stop.
Nowak. I'll be gone by the weekend, I expect.
Frank. I wasn't sure you'd come this way.
Morning, Frank. Neither of us slept, by the look.
Frank. If you want to talk, I've ten minutes.
Hello, Frank. I'm still here. Don't read into it.
Frank. Don't get yourself talked about.
Evening, Frank. I should be on the train by now.
Frank. You're not what I expected.
Frank, you're wet. Stand under here.
Frank. I didn't think you'd stay this long.
Careful! I've a bag.
Watch it. I've enough on today.
Do be careful.
Don't. I'm not in the mood.
Oh, for God's sake.
Excuse me, please.
Excuse me? Is there a rush?
Oh. It's you. Fine.
Careful. I bruise.
Of course it's raining. It always did.
Rain. That's the train delayed.
Typical. I came without an umbrella.
There it goes.
That's welcome home, then.
Drizzle. I grew up in worse.
A fine rain. Hook weather.
Now it pours. Naturally.
Right, I'm getting out of this.
Wet pavements and wet faces. That's the Hook.
I'd forgotten how it never stops raining here.
My coat's ruined. It was my good one.
Nobody walks in this. I'm walking.
Every gutter on this street was always blocked.
Drizzle. Doesn't even count as weather.
It gets in your hair. I remember.
I'll wait it out under here.
Rain like that, nothing moves. Not even me.
That's a window gone. I know the sound.
Glass. I'd know it anywhere.
Somebody's been broken into.
Not my business. Not any more.
Who does that? Who does that here?
Typical. The one week I'm back.
Somebody ought to ring the police.
Stay inside, whoever you are.
Somebody ran. I didn't see who.
A shape. I was checking the time.
Somebody passed. I couldn't see who.
I'm not a witness. I saw a shape.
Somebody. In a hurry. That's all.
Something moved. I looked away.
I'd not like to say. I wasn't looking properly.
A figure by the wall. Gone.
I got a clear look. I won't pretend otherwise.
I had a good look. Then it was gone.
Hey! I saw you! Stop!
I couldn't say who. I'd know the face.
That face. I'm keeping it.
They saw me looking. I didn't look away.
I'll remember that face. I've a memory.
No name. But I'll know the face again.
Not here. Not now.
I saw nothing. I was elsewhere.
I'm leaving soon. I want no part.
Lower your voice. Please.
People are looking. Walk.
The less I know, the better.
I'm saying nothing. I'm not stopping.
It's always the same round here. Eyes everywhere.
Sorry. I've been away too long.
I used to know. It's changed.
The cab office would know. I wouldn't.
That way, maybe. Don't hold me to it.
I'm not stopping. Ask somebody local.
I'm not from round here any more.
Ask at the chapel. Father Walsh knows every street.
Ask the dispatcher. She'll know.
I must go.
I've a train to catch.
Be careful.
Take it easy. I mean that.
Right. I'm off.
Goodbye.
It's slick out there. Careful.
Go home. It's late.
